participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check on form DCI-77, dated within the past 30 days. Submit form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature through the state portal. The Iowa Judicial Branch instructions state a request costs $15. Obtain it and then file the § 901C.3 application promptly, because it expires after 30 days.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you signed the release authorization on the DCI request?" against Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check on form DCI-77, dated within the past 30 days, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Release authorization signature — DCI-77, RELEASE AUTHORIZATION SIGNATURE.
Payment — DCI-76 billing form.
Criminal history result fields — Returned record.
Notarisation of results — DCI-77, 'I am required to have the results notarized'.
The subject of the request signs the DCI-77 release authorization. Without it a complete record may not be releasable under Iowa Code chapter 692.2.

$15 per Iowa criminal history record check, charged per last name. Each last name requested requires a separate request form and payment. Cash, cheques, money orders and MasterCard, Visa or Discover are accepted, or a pre-paid DCI account.
None identified.

Submit the request form and billing form with the fee to the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation by mail, fax, email or in person. Phone requests are not accepted. Every request must include at minimum a first name, last name and exact date of birth for the subject.

A circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected. ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order. County totals commonly run from roughly $60 to $235; McLean County publishes $136, comprising a $60 filing fee, a $60 state police fee and $16 for four certified copies. Treat every figure as county-specific.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

No $250 solicitor administrative fee, unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of the plea arrangement under which the defendant pled guilty and was sentenced to other charges, in which case the $250 applies. No $25 SLED verification fee. No $35 clerk of court filing fee where the charge was discharged, dismissed, nolle prossed or the applicant was acquitted.

The § 17-22-940(A)(1) exemption is the operative relief on this route and is automatic rather than discretionary. The solicitor may waive the $250 fee only where a person has been falsely accused as a result of identity theft, § 17-22-940(J). Each solicitor's office also maintains a private donation account which may defray up to fifty per cent of the administrative fee on a first-come first-served basis, § 17-22-940(A)(2).

Two steps with different actors. The participant requests the packet from the office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court. participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable. On this track specifically, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.

In-window: a request to the trial court under art. 55A.201, with notice to the state, accompanied by the art. 55A.253 information package. Out-of-window: a verified ex parte petition filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.

It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.

Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.

requiredBeforeFiling: Check your answer to "What is the docket number? A separate petition is needed for each unrelated offence and for each county." against Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "What exactly were you convicted of — the offence name and, if you have it, the statute section? Vermont's qualifying-crime screen runs on the exact section, not the offence label." against Vermont Crime Information Center criminal conviction record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that restitution and surcharges are paid in full on every conviction. Ask the Restitution Unit for a current balance and the sentencing court for any outstanding surcharge. This is the one Vermont track with a filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e), read at source on 2026-08-06, the $90 filing fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a) and does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions. Two currency problems attach and are carried as a release blocker rather than resolved: § 1431(e) still cross-references 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(1)(C), a subdivision Act 60 eliminated, and the Judiciary's own gloss that the fee applies where the offence was committed at 25 or older has no anchor in the current § 7602 text. The packet therefore states that a fee applies on this track and directs the participant to the Judiciary fee page rather than asserting an amount or an age condition.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county. Complete Form 200-00331, Request for Criminal Record Search, and email, mail or hand deliver it to the court in each county. A separate request is required for each county, and there is a fee. participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the docket number? A separate petition is needed for each unrelated offence and for each county." against Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Vermont Crime Information Center criminal conviction record. Request the statewide conviction record from VCIC online, by mail, by email or in person. There is a fee, which moves and must be read from VCIC at intake rather than stored. The Judiciary record gives the docket and disposition detail the petition needs; the VCIC record gives the statewide picture the qualifying-crime and prior-conviction screens need.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Vermont Crime Information Center

No filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) the $90 fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), and expressly does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions.

Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.

Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.
